title: Bastille Day Storm - July 2000 (1140 km/s)
peak_caption: Peak Kp 9, min Bz -60 nT, min SYM-H -326 nT
key_moments: KEY MOMENTS: shock 14:45 UT 15 Jul (6 -> 24 nPa) | Bz min -60 nT at 19:55 UT 15 Jul | wind peaks 1137 km/s 22:05 UT 15 Jul | Kp 9 from 18:35 UT 15 Jul | SYM-H min -326 nT at 21:55 UT 15 Jul | Bz below -10 nT for 6 h

physics.magnetopause: Lin et al. 2010 (doi:10.1029/2009JA014235) 3-D surface - cusp indentations, dipole-tilt and dawn-dusk asymmetry - on a subsolar distance blended C2 to Shue et al. 1998 outside Lin's fitted box (Bz -15..+5 nT, Pd 1..16 nPa), where Lin's inputs are clamped
physics.bow_shock: Slavin & Holzer 1981 conic, Farris & Russell 1994 standoff, ratio bounded at BS_RATIO_MAX, radius scaled per azimuth by the magnetopause's own shape so the sheath cannot invert
physics.aberration: applied to the magnetopause evaluation and the wind's upstream direction only - Tsyganenko field lines stay in plain GSM, the frame they are fitted in
physics.field_line_clip: open lines cut at the DRAWN magnetopause, looked up in 2-D (theta, phi) on the export lattice itself, so the clip and the exported shell are the same surface by construction - a theta-only profile is the wrong boundary at the flank, where the radius varies more than tenfold with azimuth. Closed lines are NOT cut (both feet on the Earth is what defines them) and any that sit outside are counted as a real field-model/boundary-model disagreement
physics.obj_frame: yup-precompensated: shell .obj vertices and normals written (x, z, -y) so Digistar's Y-up import draws them in the export frame
physics.wind_shock: Rankine-Hugoniot jump at the fast-magnetosonic Mach number, obliquity-weighted and faded out past the Slavin & Holzer asymptote where the conic is clamped rather than computed
physics.extra_layers: RingCurrent (energy measured from Dst/SYM-H via Dessler-Parker-Sckopke, radial geometry is climatology), Plasmasphere (plasmapause from Carpenter & Anderson 1992 doi:10.1029/91JA01548, axisymmetric - no duskside plume), IMFLines (drape convected through the wind's own flow field, reconnection marked where Kan & Lee 1979 doi:10.1029/GL006i007p00577 gives a non-zero merging rate - quasi-steady, no induction equation)

aurora_label: Modeled auroral oval - Kp 9 (statistical Kp model, not an observation)
talking_points: WATCH: the CME shock from the X5.7 flare hits L1 about 14:37 UT on 15 Jul - the pressure jumps roughly tenfold and the magnetopause and bow shock crush inward within a step
PHYSICS: Bz swings to about -60 nT. Southward IMF reconnects at the nose, dayside field lines peel back into the tail - watch the tail lines stretch and the oval expand
IMPACT: Kp 9, Dst about -300 nT. Aurora seen as far south as Texas - the ASCA X-ray satellite lost attitude control and never observed again, radio and GPS were disrupted

sheath_gap_re.note: distance from a magnetosheath parcel to the magnetopause, over parcels inside the bow shock only
